topic: Finding and fixing graph-scale and shape-attribute errors

traps.desc: left the uneven scale alone and kept the label the student wrote

problems.desc: (b) instructor-judged. A full-credit answer says the steps on a scale must all be the same size, and that an uneven step makes the marks sit in the wrong places so the plot cannot be read fairly. An answer that only says the label is wrong, without saying why equal steps matter, is not full credit.

traps.desc: counted the tick marks along the scale instead of the marks stacked above 3

problems.desc: (b) instructor-judged. A full-credit answer names the mistake: the student counted numbers on the scale instead of counting the marks stacked above the number 3. Saying only that the answer is wrong, or restating the correct answer, is not full credit.

traps.desc: assumed that four equal sides must mean four square corners

problems.desc: (b) instructor-judged. A full-credit answer says four equal sides is not enough: a square also needs four square corners, and the tilted shape has none, so equal sides alone do not make a square. An answer that only says the shape is tilted, with no mention of corners, is not full credit.

traps.desc: added the numbers printed along the scale instead of counting the marks

problems.desc: (b) instructor-judged. A full-credit answer says the numbers on the scale are the values borrowed, not the students, and that the students are counted by counting the marks. An answer that only gives the right total, with no account of what the scale numbers actually mean, is not full credit.

traps.desc: added the greatest and least values instead of subtracting them

problems.desc: (b) instructor-judged. A full-credit answer says a difference is found by subtracting, not adding, and that the greatest and least values are read off the scale. An answer that only writes the correct number is not full credit.

problems.slot: (a) pairs of parallel sides on that shape

traps.desc: assumed every four-sided shape has two pairs of parallel sides

problems.desc: (b) instructor-judged. A full-credit answer says only the top and bottom sides of that shape stay the same distance apart, while the two slanted sides lean towards each other, so there is one pair and not two. An answer that only names the shape, with no reference to which sides are parallel, is not full credit.

traps.desc: counted the tick marks instead of the gaps between them

problems.desc: (b) instructor-judged. A full-credit answer says that when one gap is wider than another, equal counts of marks take up different amounts of room, so a column can look bigger than a taller one and the plot gives a false picture. An answer that only says it looks untidy is not full credit.

(b) instructor-judged. A full-credit answer gives a method that does not start over: compare the height of each column on the copy with the height of the same column on the correct plot, and the one column that is one mark short shows which value was left out. An answer that says only to count everything again is not full credit.
problems.slot: (b) how to find the missing value
